```{r sanitize-datatable}
# Create a function to clean up data frames
sanitize_datatable <- function(df, ...) {
  # Remove dashes from row names and column names which cause wrapping
  DT::datatable(df, ...,
    rownames = gsub("-", "_", rownames(df)),
    colnames = gsub("-", "_", colnames(df))
  )
}
```

```{r load data, eval=FALSE}
seurat <- qread("results/12.3_astro_cluster_res0.15.qs")
seurat <- subset(seurat,
                 astro_cluster_projected != "13")

# Create new column
seurat$astro_clusters_grouped <- seurat$astro_cluster_projected
seurat$astro_clusters_grouped[seurat$astro_clusters_grouped %in% c(5, 7)] <- "5_7"

# Order
order <- seurat$astro_cluster_projected %>%
  unique() %>% as.numeric() %>% sort() %>%
  as.character()

idx5 <- match("5", order)
order_grouped <- append(order[!order %in% c("5", "7")], "5_7", after = idx5 - 1)

# Factorize
seurat$astro_clusters_grouped <- factor(seurat$astro_clusters_grouped,
                                        levels = order_grouped)

name_astro <- paste0("astro_", 1:length(order_grouped))
map_vec <- setNames(name_astro, order_grouped)

# Apply to your Seurat object column
seurat$name_astro_clusters <- map_vec[as.character(seurat$astro_clusters_grouped)] %>% unname()
seurat$name_astro_clusters <- factor(seurat$name_astro_clusters,
                                     levels = name_astro)
```

# Cell Type Counts

We again exclude AGHD16 from analysis as its clustering is not consistent with the other samples.

```{r subset-data, eval=FALSE}
seurat_laminar <- subset(seurat, general_code != 'AGHD16')
seurat_laminar@meta.data <- seurat_laminar@meta.data %>%
  mutate(age_group = factor(age_group,
                            levels = c("young", "middle", "old")))
seurat_laminar_meta <- seurat_laminar@meta.data
```

Most of the cell types have >50 cells per sample, meaning that attempting analysis of cell type proportion at this level of granularity is reasonable. We note that, for cell types with <50 cells, statistical results may be less reliable.

# sccomp {.tabset}

To test for differential cell composition we use [sccomp](https://github.com/MangiolaLaboratory/sccomp) a method for differential composition and variability analyses that jointly models data count distribution, compositionality, group-specific variability, and proportion mean–variability association, being aware of outliers.

Our model includes age group (old vs young or middle vs young). Results are computed per cortical layer.

```{r compute-sccomp, eval = !file.exists('results/12.12_sccomp_results_by_layer.qs')}
cortical_layers <- seurat_laminar$cortical_layer_v2 %>%
  unique() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  sort()

sccomp_results_list     <- list()
sccomp_results_sex_list <- list()

for (layer in cortical_layers) {
  seurat_sub <- subset(seurat_laminar, cortical_layer_v2 == layer)

  set.seed(1454944673L)
  sccomp_results_list[[layer]] <- seurat_sub |>
    sccomp_estimate(
      formula_composition = ~age_group,
      .sample  = sample,
      .cell_group = name_astro_clusters,
      bimodal_mean_variability_association = TRUE,
      cores = 1,
      variational_inference = FALSE,
      verbose = FALSE
    ) |>
    sccomp_remove_outliers(cores = 1, verbose = FALSE) |>
    sccomp_test() %>%
    mutate(cortical_layer_v2 = layer)
}

qsave(sccomp_results_list, 'results/12.12_sccomp_results_by_layer.qs')
```

```{r}
  # ── posterior predictive check plots ─────────────────────────────────────
  cat(paste0(

    "The blue boxplots represent the posterior predictive check. ",
    "If the model is descriptively adequate for the data, the blue boxplots ",
    "should roughly overlay the black boxplots, which represent the observed data. ",
    "The color coding represents the significant associations.\n\n"
  ))
  cat("**We see that the blue boxplots vary from the black boxplots quite a bit, ",

```

```{r process-results}
sccomp_results_list <- qread('results/12.12_sccomp_results_by_layer.qs')

# Helper: compute proportional fold changes and join with FDR results
compute_result_combined <- function(sccomp_result) {
  fc <- lapply(c('old', 'middle'), function(x) {
    sccomp_result |>
      sccomp_proportional_fold_change(
        formula_composition = ~age_group,
        from = "young",
        to   = x
      ) %>%
      mutate(parameter = paste0('age_group', x),
             to = x,
             from = "young")
  }) %>% bind_rows()

  sccomp_result %>%
    filter(factor == 'age_group') %>%
    dplyr::select(name_astro_clusters, parameter, c_FDR,
                  cortical_layer_v2) %>%
    left_join(fc, by = c("name_astro_clusters", "parameter")) %>%
    arrange(c_FDR)
}

all_results_combined <- lapply(sccomp_results_list, compute_result_combined)
```

```{r display-sccomp, results='asis', fig.height=8, fig.width=12}
for (layer in names(sccomp_results_list)) {

  cat(paste0("\n\n## ", layer, "\n\n"))

  # ── full results table ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  result_combined <- all_results_combined[[layer]]
  print(htmltools::tagList(sanitize_datatable(result_combined)))
  cat("\n\n")

  # ── significant results ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  cat("Significant results:\n\n")
  print(htmltools::tagList(
    sanitize_datatable(
      result_combined %>%
        subset(c_FDR < 0.05) %>%
        dplyr::select(name_astro_clusters, cortical_layer_v2,
                      to, from, 
                      proportion_fold_change, c_FDR)
    )
  ))
  cat("\n\n")

  # print(
  #   sccomp_results_list[[layer]] |> sccomp_boxplot(factor = "age_group")
  # )
  # cat("\n\n")

  print(
    sccomp_results_list[[layer]] |>
      sccomp_boxplot(factor = "age_group", remove_unwanted_effects = TRUE) +
      facet_wrap(~name_astro_clusters, nrow = 2, scales = 'free_y') +
      theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
      ggtitle(paste("Layer", layer))
  )
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

# Conclusions {.tabset}

Based upon sccomp, comparing `young` to `old`, the following populations show a significant change in proportion per cortical layer. A positive fold change indicates more cells in `old` compared to `young`.

```{r conclusions, results='asis'}
for (layer in names(all_results_combined)) {
  cat(paste0("\n\n## ", layer, "\n\n"))

  sig <- all_results_combined[[layer]] %>%
    subset(c_FDR < 0.05) %>%
    dplyr::select(name_astro_clusters, cortical_layer_v2,
                  from, to,
                  proportion_fold_change, statement, c_FDR)

  print(kable(sig))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```
